name: Zolak
funding: Founders' private contributions, residency subscriptions, event rentals, a crypto bar and donations; states it does not take grants
watch: 150 m2 'micro art residence' and community venue at Vytenio g. 50D (former ELFA factory), opened 14 Jun 2025 by Piotr Markielau, Alina Nahornaja and Siarhei Hudzilin: residencies, screenings, discussions, coworking, raves, sauna.
records_note: Zolak's site lists spaces, prices and rules, with no annual report, accounts, funder names or board.

name: Museo de la Ciudad de México
funding: Public museum run by the Mexico City Ministry of Culture.
watch: A federal judge suspended Fabián Cháirez's show in April 2025 after an amparo suit. The city culture ministry defended the show.
records_note: The museum's site and its Culture Secretariat's site did not connect, so reports, accounts, funders and board could not be checked.

name: Colección FEMSA
funding: Corporate art collection of FEMSA, founded 1977 and managed by FEMSA staff. FEMSA runs OXXO stores and the Coca-Cola FEMSA bottler.
watch: Residents of San Cristóbal de las Casas, Chiapas marched in 2017 to cancel the Coca-Cola FEMSA plant's water concession; permits cost 2,600 pesos each.
records_note: The collection is part of FEMSA, which files an annual report and a 20-F with audited accounts and names its board.

name: Museo de los Pintores Oaxaqueños
funding: State museum run by the Oaxaca state patronato for cultural and tourist units.
watch: Temporary exhibitions only, no permanent collection. The state government began rehabilitating the colonial building. No protest or censorship found.
records_note: The museum is run by Oaxaca's state cultural patronage board, whose sites did not connect, so reports, accounts, funders and board are unchecked.

name: Centro Cultural Tijuana
funding: Federal state company under Mexico's culture ministry. Modified budget MXN 132.9M for January to September 2025, of which MXN 88.0M accrued. A private patronato supports it.
watch: More than 250 Tijuana artists and writers boycotted the centre and its director Virgilio Muñoz for about three years, to 2011.
why_flagged: Federal state company under Mexico's culture ministry. Modified budget MXN 132.9M for January to September 2025, of which MXN 88.0M accrued. A private patronato supports it.
records_note: The centre posts federal budget and spending reports by quarter, but no annual report, funder list or board.

name: Zanabazar Museum of Fine Art
funding: Mongolian state museum (founded 1966) listed by the National Centre for Cultural Heritage; UNESCO preservation partner.
watch: Roster not checked. No funder list found; zanabazarmuseum.org is now a gambling spam domain, not the museum. No controversy found.
records_note: Its own site is down; parent body NCCH posts activity reports for 2006 to 2022 but no accounts, funders or board.

name: Fundação Fernando Leite Couto
funding: Sponsors in 2025: Moza Banco, Nedbank, Standard Bank and the Calouste Gulbenkian Foundation. Prize partners include Óbidos council, the Portugal-Mozambique Chamber of Commerce and Camões.
watch: The Gulbenkian Foundation, endowed by oilman Calouste Gulbenkian, backed a 2025 drama workshop and is a listed sponsor.
why_flagged: Sponsors in 2025: Moza Banco, Nedbank, Standard Bank and the Calouste Gulbenkian Foundation. Prize partners include Óbidos council, the Portugal-Mozambique Chamber of Commerce and Camões.
records_note: It posts activity reports for 2022 to 2025, accounts for 2019 and 2023 to 2025, a 2025 sponsor list and its three founders.

name: National Art Gallery of Namibia
funding: State-owned art gallery. Bank Windhoek partners on its 2025/2026 Triennial.
watch: In March 2014 the gallery asked artist Paolo Solari Bozzi to withdraw photos of Himba girls; he pulled the whole show. The gallery denied censorship.
why_flagged: In March 2014 the gallery asked artist Paolo Solari Bozzi to withdraw photos of Himba girls; he pulled the whole show. The gallery denied censorship.
records_note: NAGN posts annual reports for 2019/20 to 2024/25 with audited statements, names its seven trustees, and names its strategic partners in the latest report.

name: Kathmandu Triennale
funding: Siddhartha Arts Foundation with Nepal Academy of Fine Arts (2026); 2022 edition backed by embassies, Saraf Foundation, Gorkha Brewery, Himalayan Bank, Toyota.
watch: Full corporate sponsor list not verified. 2026 supporters page shows only organisers, patrons 'No data found'. 2022 roster (archived) read: no excluded names. No controversy found.
records_note: The current Triennale site lists only its two organisers as supporters, with patrons empty, and posts no reports, accounts, funder list or board.

name: National Museum, Lagos
funding: Federal Government through the National Commission for Museums and Monuments; IHS Nigeria, a telecom-tower company, funded a 2026 renovation. A Ford Foundation refit stalled.
watch: Reopened April 2026 after renovation. No NNPC, Shell, TotalEnergies or Dangote money found.
records_note: A federal museum with no records of its own; the parent commission's site posts no annual reports, accounts, funder list or governing council.

name: Henie Onstad Kunstsenter
funding: Main partner Stiftelsen DNV, NOK 2M a year; founded on Niels Onstad's shipping fortune; Norwegian state.
watch: DNV certifies oil and gas assets; full roster not seen.
records_note: It posts annual reports for 2013 to 2025 naming funders and its board; accounts for 2023 to 2025 are in the Norwegian register.

name: Kunsthall Stavanger
watch: In Norway's oil capital; no Equinor or Aker BP link found, roster unseen.
records_note: It posts annual reports 2018 to 2025, an undated supporter list and its board; accounts for 2023 to 2025 sit in the Norwegian register.
